recent_commits.body:
R/data_check_helpers.R — two shared, package-level helpers (so both the module and the converter can call them):

.osd_safe_code() — spec-valid code sanitizer.
.osd_code_and_provenance() — the three-tier provenance/code minting (dictionary → bare official code or curated METACHECK-; manuscript → METACHECK-; self-generated → METACHECK-GEN-), each with a human-readable provenance sentence.
inst/modules/codebook_check.R — rewrote .scales_to_osd(scale_groups, columns_df, labels_df, dict):

Spec-conformant structure: osd_version, definition.{scale_info, likert_options, items}, translations.en, plus a namespaced definition.metacheck block for provenance/confidence/source (kept out of the spec objects).
likert_options lets the codebook lead — decodes value_labels for range + anchor labels (source:"codebook"); falls back to observed min/max/n_unique from data_check stats (source:"observed"); omitted entirely when nothing is scale-shaped (no invention).
translations.en carries codebook item wording; text_key points at it per spec.
Named groups flagged write=TRUE; unnamed detections write=FALSE (report-only, no file).
R/psychds-convert.R — the file writer + cross-reference:

.osd_write_scales() writes one scales/{CODE}/{CODE}.osd per named scale (pretty JSON) under the dataset root.
.osd_write_readme_section() appends a "Psychometric scales" section to the root README.md explaining the three provenance markers and listing every scale (your "general README" decision).
Added metacheck:scale code + source to variableMeasured, so Psych-DS variables cross-reference their OSD definition.
n_scales added to the return list and completion message.

recent_commits.message: docs(evidence): complete 8-canary B6 result + W0o implementation blocker measured
recent_commits.body:
B6 verdict updated with the full canary set: 7 heading regressions across 6 of
8 canaries (xiao adds "## Evaluation"; maier and plos_med are the only clean
ones). Zero byte-identical. Table counts unchanged everywhere, so the damage is
purely to the document outline, not a table-capture trade. Verdict unchanged:
NO-GO, default stays OFF.

W0o hyphen recovery was prototyped against the LayoutDoc that normalize.py
already receives as dropped_minus_layout, so it could be wired exactly like
W0h/W0m. It returns 0 rewrites, and per the "a zero is a claim to be tested"
rule that was diagnosed rather than accepted:

  131 line-final-hyphen pairs found, only 26 correct, and the target
  ('Well','Being') is NOT among them. The wrong pairs are scrambled across
  columns -- indepen+Background, well+Corresponding, pur+beyond.

Cause: bucketing pdfplumber chars into visual lines by y merges the two columns,
so "the next line" grabs the other column's text. This is the B6 interleave
problem reappearing inside the fix's own helper -- the same root cause that makes
70% of the S7 population garbage. pdftotext -bbox gets reading order right;
the pdfplumber char stream alone does not.

So W0o cannot ship as a drop-in sibling of W0h/W0m. It needs a pdftotext -bbox
word channel threaded into normalize (tractable, but a new extraction channel),
NOT column-aware line assembly over LayoutDoc (that is B6, just declined).

The gate itself remains validated; only its implementation route is blocked.

recent_commits.body:
The user approved a staged go conditional on "no regressions or issues". The
8-canary rendered-output read is that gate, and it fails.

Six heading regressions across five of six canaries compared so far, two of
which are content corruption rather than reflow:

  efendic  -- "### Author Biographies" is WELDED INTO a reference-list line:
              "...https://doi.org/10.1111/ jcom.12071 Author Biographies Emir
              Efendic is a postdoctoral scholar..." Three properly separated
              blocks with the flag OFF; one spliced run with it ON.
  ar_apa   -- "### Participants" absent from the ON render entirely.
  chandrashekar / chan_feldman / ip_feldman / efendic -- headings demoted to
              body text or absorbed into table cells.

plos_med_1 is clean.

Every one of these preserves the word multiset perfectly, which is exactly why
run 7's 58-document / 0-words-lost text-channel measurement could not see them.
That result is not contradicted -- it was never capable of detecting reordering,
as the evidence pack itself said. The rendered word count is equally misleading:
the raw diff reads "560 words lost" but most is HTML escaping and table filler.
Neither word count decides this; reading the structure does.

Recorded honestly: the flag genuinely IMPROVES some table rendering (ip_feldman
Table 5 goes from an orphaned vertical value dump to a correct aligned table).
The change is not uniformly bad -- it is net-unsafe, which is the more dangerous
shape and why an isolated improvement was never sufficient evidence.

Third correct rejection of this class at the rendered-reading gate. Flags stay

block-level structural-preservation guard inside the splice, mirroring the
existing unconditional word-preservation guard one level up.

recent_commits.message: docs(evidence): hyphenation gate MEASURED — both queued fixes were mis-specified
recent_commits.body:
Run 8 set out to execute the two queued hyphenation fixes. Measuring them first
changed both, so this lands the evidence before any code.

1. The S7 widening, as specified, would CORRUPT the corpus. The tolerant
   separator matches 43 sites across 40 papers, but 30 of them (70%, all from
   one 3-column paper) are column-interleave garbage, not hyphenation:
   conspir-|that, theo-|imply, phenom-|experiment. Geometry proves it —
   `conspir-` ends at x=288 and `that` begins at x=306 on the SAME visual line,
   a jump across the gutter. The true continuation is conspir-|acy. Widening
   would create ~30 corruptions to repair ~13 real breaks. The dead-code
   diagnosis stands; the prescribed remedy does not.

2. The attestation gate, explicitly banned by the prior audit, is the only
   discriminator that works. The ban rested on "every no-hyphen wellbeing here
   is itself a line-break artifact" — true about the glued form's ORIGIN, but
   the inference drawn from it (no independent attestation exists) is false:
   the document has 61 genuinely inline `well-being`, 0 spanning a newline.

3. Codex's recommended gate (capital right fragment) is UNSAFE — it fires on
   minor-We, percep-Minority, the-Personal, Ameri-To, con-M,
   electroencephalog-Action, all column interleave. Rejected on measurement per
   the "reproduction decides it" rule. Two attempts at a column-continuity
   guard to rescue it both failed and are recorded as a dead end.

Final gate, measured over 4,506 line-final-hyphen sites in 46 papers:
    fire IFF inline_hyphenated(A-B) > genuine_glued_tokens(AB)
where genuine_glued counts AB as a single word token in the -bbox LAYOUT
channel — asking the layout channel is what keeps the glued count non-circular,
since the text channel's glued forms are the artifacts under repair.

168 fires (3.73%), correct on every decisive case: accepts Well-Being (7/0),
well-being (53/0), in-group (17/2); rejects out-group (2/7), inter-group (1/4).
One known FP: New-York, a publisher typo the page actually prints.

Triple-verified: measurement + codex (dissented, refuted on data) + an
adversarial Sonnet pass that reproduced every number, confirmed the page by
300dpi raster, and found a URL false-positive class neither other pass raised
(0 of 168 fires, so incidental — hardening noted, plus a separate open defect
for mid-line glued URL hyphens).

No code changed.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): strip BIDI FORMAT marks in S6 (v2.4.125)
recent_commits.body:
An invisible U+200E LEFT-TO-RIGHT MARK survived normalization into
rendered output immediately after a citation's closing paren
(xiao_2021_crsp: `Connolly, Reb, and Kausel (2013)<U+200E>`).

The S6 invisible-character block already stripped U+200B/C/D and
U+FEFF but SKIPPED U+200E/U+200F -- an omission in a sequence, not a
design decision. Now also strips U+2060 WORD JOINER, same class.

This is a CORRECTNESS defect, not cosmetics. An invisible character
inside rendered output breaks STRING EQUALITY and SEARCH for every
downstream consumer: a citation checker comparing `(2013)` against
`(2013)<LRM>` sees a mismatch it cannot see on screen -- and docpluck's
output feeds exactly such consumers (citelink, CitationGuard). Same
rationale already recorded for the adjacent U+00AD strip ("invisible,
breaks search").

NORMALIZATION_VERSION -> 1.9.50.

Verification:
- 9 new tests, each watched FAILING at unfixed HEAD first (7 failed /
  2 passed -- the 2 passing prove the pre-existing U+200B/C/D/FEFF
  strips still work, so the red was specific to the new class).
- Strip effectiveness verified on a synthetic positive BEFORE the
  guard-diff, so a zero result is trustworthy rather than a false green.
- Corpus guard-diff, all 101 PDFs: 100 byte-identical BY CONSTRUCTION
  (they contain no bidi mark at all); the 1 touched is xiao, with
  exactly the 2 reported marks. Zero false positives possible.
- Idempotency + normalize guards: 41 passed, 0 failed.
- Full suite: 2015 passed, 190 skipped, 3 xfailed, 0 failed.
  Reconciles exactly as 2006 pre-existing + 9 new; skips and xfails
  unchanged, so zero behavioural drift.

Found via the run-7 triage of the open canary findings.

recent_commits.message: docs(audit): DP-3 cross-project adjudication — verdict upheld, MECHANISM REFUTED
recent_commits.body:
First item of the queued cross-project re-audit, chosen for blast radius: a
docpluck->ESCIcheck REPLY document where one project told another "not our defect".

REPLY_FROM_DOCPLUCK_2026-06-25 stated the root cause as "the eta-squared-p glyph
lives in a font with no ToUnicode CMap (NotoSerif-Regular uni:no), so both pdftotext
AND pdfplumber decode it as a space". Measured on collabra.90203 p.1:

- NotoSerif-Regular carries 561 char objects on that page and ALL 561 are the SPACE
  character -- it is the document's space font, not a symbol font.
- Its space widths are 2.08-3.90pt (mean 2.43); ZERO exceed 5pt, while the symbol's
  ink spans 7.98pt. No NotoSerif space is wide enough to be the symbol.
- The only char object near the gap is a NotoSerif space at x0=229.97 -- the ordinary
  space BEFORE the '=' at x=232.31, i.e. after the symbol, not in place of it.
- The symbol is 4 filled bezier curves (fill=True, no fontname) with NO char object.

So the verdict (OCR/shape-recognition tier for body prose) is RIGHT, but the stated
mechanism is REFUTED. Codex on why that still causes harm: the rationale teaches the
wrong failure mode, so a consumer would attempt ToUnicode recovery, glyph-name
mapping, extractor tuning or post-processing NotoSerif spaces -- all of which target
the ordinary space before '=' and can never recover drawn curves. The distinction
that matters is "text encoded badly" vs "ink that is not text".

PROPAGATION CONFIRMED. REPLY_TO_DOCPLUCK_2026-06-26 records ESCIcheck replying "we
confirmed your OCR-tier won't-fix: the prose reads '( = .000...)' with no eta
anywhere" -- the identical circular check. A wrong rationale crossed the repo
boundary and was ratified by the receiving project using the same flawed method.
That is exactly the shape this audit exists to catch.

Both documents now carry correction blocks (in ESCIcheckapp, a separate repo). The
table-side fields.eta2 binding is unaffected and remains correct. A deterministic
vector-path recogniser remains a viable NON-OCR route.

recent_commits.body:
Publisher furniture was splitting a sentence in half, and a keyword list was
being read as the Introduction's first sentence.

NORMALIZATION_VERSION -> 1.9.49; SECTIONING_VERSION -> 1.2.4.

1. Wrapped-CONTACT block (normalize.py, P0)

xiao_2021_crsp rendered the T&F correspondence footer INSIDE a body sentence:
"The target and the / CONTACT Gilad Feldman / Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR /
competitor form a core choice set". The v2.4.6 rule requires CONTACT + name +
email on ONE line; T&F column-wraps the block so each lands on its own line.

Four of the block's six lines were ALREADY stripped by sibling patterns, so
this was a PARTIAL strip -- worse than none, because it removes exactly the
lines that made the block recognisable as furniture and welds the residue into
prose. When auditing a strip rule, check what its NEIGHBOURS already remove.

Keyed on the structural signature (line-initial all-caps CONTACT followed only
by a personal name), never paper identity. A _CONTACT_NON_NAME_WORDS veto keeps
nav furniture ("CONTACT Details Below"). The orphaned "<City>, <Region>" tail is
removed ONLY by adjacency to a dropped opener -- never on its own shape, since a
bare "Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR" is ordinary prose (a test pins that it survives
alone). The wrapped pattern deliberately does NOT live in
_PAGE_FOOTER_LINE_PATTERNS: the generic any()-match would drop vetoed lines
before the veto branch could run.

2. KEYWORDS label/value split (sections/core.py)

The keywords section came out as 10 chars ('KEYWORDS\n\n') while its values
became the synthesized Introduction's opening line. The cut-at-first-"\n\n"
landed BETWEEN the label and its own values. General rule: a "cut at the first
separator" heuristic needs a post-condition on what the cut LEAVES, not only
where it lands.

render.py's _demote_metadata_label_headings blamed this on "R4 column-aware
extraction reorders the front-matter" -- false on both counts (the raw text has
label and values adjacent and in order, and "Introduction" does not occur in
that paper's source at all; the heading is synthesized). Comment corrected.

A bare pytest walked tmp/ and collected 6 scratch files -> 10 collection ERRORs
and a test count that depended on leftover debris (run5=1962 vs run6=2295, not
comparable), defeating the project's "a shrinking test count is a failure"
tripwire. testpaths pinned -> stable 2199 = 2155 pre-existing + 44 new.

recent_commits.message: docpluck-iterate: add rule 20a — how to survey, and when a survey cannot help
recent_commits.body:
Rule 20 says "survey the corpus before you write a threshold". Run 5 obeyed it
and still got the survey wrong TWICE, in opposite directions, so the rule needed
the missing half: how to build a survey whose number means anything.

(a) Survey through the REAL entry point. The W0i survey fed raw pdftotext lines
    through a function that production only ever calls on Camelot table cells,
    and reported ~85 hits in 10 papers -- including a paper's TITLE. The
    production render for that same paper had ZERO. Overstated ~10x; reporting it
    would have described a catastrophe that does not exist and over-engineered
    the guard to match. Red flag encoded: a hit-rate wildly above the audit that
    motivated the work means the harness is over-broad.

(b) A ZERO result must be falsified before it is believed. The first W0d survey
    returned zero firings corpus-wide -- a comfortable all-clear that was pure
    artifact (W0d runs whole-document; the raw-text channel puts each cell on its
    own line, so an estimate and its CI never share a line).

(c) Prefer a GUARD-DIFF over a hit count: render twice with the change toggled,
    so every difference is attributable. Both run-5 fixes shipped on exactly that
    evidence. When a full double-render is too slow, pre-filter by a stated
    criterion and report BOTH numbers so coverage stays auditable.

Plus the boundary condition that retires an entire approach family: if the thing
you are detecting occurs on exactly ONE row, no vote/follower/corroboration rule
can recover it. Counting the populated occurrences first would have saved two
prototypes on the plos_med column loss.

All references and factual claims re-verified against the tree before commit.

row-cluster family. Each looked excellent on its motivating paper; measurement,
not review, killed them. Recorded as a project lesson: print the winning row's
TEXT, not just its column count -- a footer, a running header and a wrapped
caption all look like "wide rows" to geometry.

recent_commits.body:
docpluck rendered an IMPOSSIBLE F-statistic. maier Table 9's row is

    Target article | 1, 114 | 2.00 | .16 | N/A | .02 | [.00, .09]

-- an F, its p, its partial eta-squared, and the CI OF THE ETA-SQUARED. W0d
(recover_minus_via_ci_pairing) repairs a font corruption where a minus is read
as '2', accepting the flip when the corrected value lands inside a paired CI and
the literal does not. It paired the F-statistic with the eta-squared's CI: -.00
is inside [.00, .09] and 2.00 is not, so it fired, and the render carried

    F = -.00

An F-statistic is a ratio of sums of squares -- non-negative by construction --
so the output was not merely wrong but arithmetically impossible. Both text
channels confirm the source reads 2.00; the library manufactured the sign.

Fix: refuse the pairing when the CI's LOWER bound is >= 0. A wholly non-negative
interval cannot contain a negative, so containment is satisfiable only
degenerately (-.00 clipping the zero edge), which is evidence of MIS-PAIRING
rather than corruption. Keying on the interval's arithmetic instead of on F
specifically covers every non-negative statistic that can sit beside a
non-negative CI (F, chi-square, R2, eta2, odds ratios, variance components)
without enumerating them, and cannot disarm a genuine recovery -- a truly
negative estimate always has a CI admitting negatives.

Evidence:
- tests written against the unfixed code and watched FAIL, then pass;
- all 31 pre-existing W0d tests stay green, incl. the efendic B-column
  recoveries the rule exists for;
- corpus guard-diff, all 152 PDFs rendered twice (guard on vs off):
  2 false positives removed (the maier article and its ESCIcheck duplicate),
  0 regressions, every other paper byte-identical;
- suite 1962 passed, 3 xfail (the P1 table defects stay armed).

Companion to the REJECTED W0b-col recovery: that failed because column consensus
is not per-record evidence. This is the converse -- per-record containment IS the
right evidence, but only when the record paired is the right one. A containment
test silently assumes the CI belongs to the token it pairs with; verify that is
arithmetically possible first.

Found by the run-5 canary audit against the AI multimodal gold.

recent_commits.message: docs(findings): measure WHY plos_med T3 loses its columns — hierarchical sub-rows
recent_commits.body:
Probing _find_stable_column_boundaries on the real Table-3 band replaces the
earlier speculation (which guessed at midpoint scatter and the region path) with
a measurement, and it kills the proposed fix:

  WORD path: valid_rows=13 threshold=7 -> stable boundaries: [] -> 1 column
  BUCKETED(3/5/8pt): still 2 columns

The word path finds ZERO stable boundaries, so the region path is NOT the
culprit. The cause is the table's shape: Table 3 is hierarchical -- the header
and one aggregate row carry all 5 columns, while 11 of 13 rows are indented
sub-rows carrying only 3 (desaturation | 3/5 | 1/4). The Rel. risk and P value
columns appear in 2/13 rows = 15%, far below COLUMN_STABILITY_FRACTION = 0.6, so
they can never reach the vote threshold. Bucketing cannot help -- the votes do
not exist to be bucketed.

Lowering the fraction is explicitly NOT the fix (rule 20): 0.6 guards against
spurious boundaries from ragged prose rows, and a threshold admitting a 15%
column admits noise corpus-wide. The correct signature is that a column declared
by the HEADER is real even when most rows leave it empty -- seed boundaries from
the header rather than letting a majority vote delete them. That is an algorithm
change to a shared detector, so it gets its own gated cycle.

Also removes the now-superseded speculative section so the doc does not
contradict its own measurement, and records the class as a project lesson: a
stability-fraction vote assumes every column is populated in most rows, which
hierarchical/sub-row tables (common in clinical papers) violate by construction --
and the failure is silent, looking like a complete table with fewer columns.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): a range bound is a number, not an interaction operator (v2.4.122)
recent_commits.body:
W0i's x-as-3 glyph recovery was rewriting RANGE BOUNDS as an operator inside
Camelot table cells. chan_feldman's Table-2 note rendered

    "Avoidance behaviour scores ranged from x to 15"

for a source that reads "from 3 to 15" -- the library DELETED a published scale
bound and wrote an operator in its place. Both text channels confirm the source
says 3; the raw-text channel rendered the same sentence correctly a hundred
lines earlier, so one document carried the same fact right and wrong at once.

Not paper-specific: any "from 3 to N" / "between 3 and N" reaching a table cell
was affected, in any publisher's paper.

Root cause: W0i's only pre-digit guard was _TIMES_REFERENCE_WORD_RE, a list of
reference NOUNS (Model|Study|Table|Figure|...) that makes "Model 3 predictor" a
genuine ordinal. "from" is not a reference noun, so the guard had nothing to
say, while "from 3 to" matches W0i's letter-space-3-space-letter signature
exactly. A vocabulary list cannot defend a grammatical position -- it is always
missing the next word.

Fix: guard on the grammatical FRAME instead. A range is from|between BEFORE the
digit AND to|and|through|until AFTER it, with BOTH halves required -- a lone
trailing "to" could be a wrapped predictor ("Attitude 3 to risk"), and a lone
leading "from" is likewise ambiguous. A frame generalises across publishers.

Evidence:
- new tests written against the unfixed code and watched FAIL, then pass;
- full-corpus pdftotext sweep (all 152 PDFs): 8 range-frame-with-3 sites across
  5 distinct articles, out of 380 range frames overall -- all 5 pinned as
  regression cases. The sweep is why the guard covers "between ... and": maier's
  Bayes factors and bmc_med_3's lesion diameters use it, and a from-only guard
  would have left them exposed;
- targeted production-path guard-diff (each paper rendered twice, guard on vs
  off, so every difference is attributable to this change): 1 false positive
  removed, 0 regressions, all 8 canaries byte-identical;
- suite: 1959 passed, 3 xfail (the two P1 pinned table defects stay armed).

recent_commits.body:
The run-4 v2.4.120/121 session's most expensive mistake and its most valuable
save both trace to this missing rule. The skill had no guidance to validate a
threshold/ratio/signature against the corpus BEFORE implementing it.

Cost when absent: the _cluster_into_rows anchor-relative fix looked excellent on
its motivating paper (chan_feldman T3 3->22 rows, T2 0->108 cells) and broke 9
real-PDF tests, because a legitimate row can be 94pt tall (xiao T4 r2).

Value when applied: four geometric discriminators (row span, max internal gap,
distinct_y, sub-line width fraction) were each falsified in minutes against the
101-PDF corpus instead of via a revert.

The rule also encodes the label-verification half, which is where the real trap
sits: hand-picked extremes ALWAYS separate, so only the decision band matters,
and labelling by provenance is a guess. Verifying the band's labels by reading
them reversed this session's conclusion TWICE before the third reading settled
it. And it requires reporting the MARGIN, not just the ordering — a correct
ordering with a 0.019 gap on six points is a rejection, not a fix.

Companion to rule 16: rule 16 says key on a structural signature; rule 20 says
prove the signature actually discriminates before shipping it.

Purely additive (2 insertions, 0 deletions). The concurrent session's
uncommitted Dropbox->Vibe path edit in this same file is deliberately NOT
included and remains in the working tree.

recent_commits.message: docs(findings): 4 geometric chain-merge discriminators tested and rejected; period-aware column overlap is the best candidate but still unsafe
recent_commits.body:
Continues the corpus-driven falsification of the row-cluster chain-merge fix.

REJECTED (all measured corpus-wide or on verified cases):
  - row span:            legit rows reach 94pt+ (xiao T4 r2)
  - max internal y-gap:  9.0pt legit vs 9.5pt chain — indistinguishable
  - distinct_y count:    continuous 2->50, classes interleave (legit 26 > chain 23)
  - subline width frac:  both classes 0.42-0.54, chain sits BETWEEN legit rows
                         (raw widths looked separable, 202-238 vs 84-150, but the
                         chain-merge regions are simply wider — normalising kills it)
  - start_at_left:       46% in BOTH classes

BEST CANDIDATE, still unsafe: column-boundary consistency. Mean Jaccard of
x-start buckets between CONSECUTIVE sub-lines gives chain 0.008-0.023 vs legit
0.21-0.28 — except xiao T4 r2 scores 0.017, deep in the chain band. That is the
exact row whose mis-splitting broke 9 tests, so this variant would repeat the
failure. It alternates data lines with CI-continuation lines, so consecutive
sub-lines never share columns but the pattern is strictly PERIODIC.

A period-aware variant (best mean Jaccard over lags 1-3) fixes xiao (0.692) and
separates the rest — but ip_feldman T10 r1 (chain) reaches 0.251 against chan T6
r2 (legit) at 0.270. A 0.019 margin on six hand-picked rows will not survive the
corpus; it needs the same survey that killed distinct_y, over rows whose class is
VERIFIED rather than assumed, and must be rejected if the margin does not widen.

Explicit guidance added: do NOT attempt a fifth geometric threshold. Remaining
viable directions are content typing and split-then-re-merge on column occupancy.

No library code changes.

highlights.message: docs(evidence): complete 8-canary B6 result + W0o implementation blocker measured
highlights.body:
B6 verdict updated with the full canary set: 7 heading regressions across 6 of
8 canaries (xiao adds "## Evaluation"; maier and plos_med are the only clean
ones). Zero byte-identical. Table counts unchanged everywhere, so the damage is
purely to the document outline, not a table-capture trade. Verdict unchanged:
NO-GO, default stays OFF.

W0o hyphen recovery was prototyped against the LayoutDoc that normalize.py
already receives as dropped_minus_layout, so it could be wired exactly like
W0h/W0m. It returns 0 rewrites, and per the "a zero is a claim to be tested"
rule that was diagnosed rather than accepted:

  131 line-final-hyphen pairs found, only 26 correct, and the target
  ('Well','Being') is NOT among them. The wrong pairs are scrambled across
  columns -- indepen+Background, well+Corresponding, pur+beyond.

Cause: bucketing pdfplumber chars into visual lines by y merges the two columns,
so "the next line" grabs the other column's text. This is the B6 interleave
problem reappearing inside the fix's own helper -- the same root cause that makes
70% of the S7 population garbage. pdftotext -bbox gets reading order right;
the pdfplumber char stream alone does not.

So W0o cannot ship as a drop-in sibling of W0h/W0m. It needs a pdftotext -bbox
word channel threaded into normalize (tractable, but a new extraction channel),
NOT column-aware line assembly over LayoutDoc (that is B6, just declined).

The gate itself remains validated; only its implementation route is blocked.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
highlights.author: Gilad Feldman

highlights.message: docs(verdict): B6 staged go step 1 FAILS the canary read — NO-GO, default stays OFF
highlights.body:
The user approved a staged go conditional on "no regressions or issues". The
8-canary rendered-output read is that gate, and it fails.

Six heading regressions across five of six canaries compared so far, two of
which are content corruption rather than reflow:

  efendic  -- "### Author Biographies" is WELDED INTO a reference-list line:
              "...https://doi.org/10.1111/ jcom.12071 Author Biographies Emir
              Efendic is a postdoctoral scholar..." Three properly separated
              blocks with the flag OFF; one spliced run with it ON.
  ar_apa   -- "### Participants" absent from the ON render entirely.
  chandrashekar / chan_feldman / ip_feldman / efendic -- headings demoted to
              body text or absorbed into table cells.

plos_med_1 is clean.

Every one of these preserves the word multiset perfectly, which is exactly why
run 7's 58-document / 0-words-lost text-channel measurement could not see them.
That result is not contradicted -- it was never capable of detecting reordering,
as the evidence pack itself said. The rendered word count is equally misleading:
the raw diff reads "560 words lost" but most is HTML escaping and table filler.
Neither word count decides this; reading the structure does.

Recorded honestly: the flag genuinely IMPROVES some table rendering (ip_feldman
Table 5 goes from an orphaned vertical value dump to a correct aligned table).
The change is not uniformly bad -- it is net-unsafe, which is the more dangerous
shape and why an isolated improvement was never sufficient evidence.

highlights.message: docs(audit): DP-3 cross-project adjudication — verdict upheld, MECHANISM REFUTED
highlights.body:
First item of the queued cross-project re-audit, chosen for blast radius: a
docpluck->ESCIcheck REPLY document where one project told another "not our defect".

REPLY_FROM_DOCPLUCK_2026-06-25 stated the root cause as "the eta-squared-p glyph
lives in a font with no ToUnicode CMap (NotoSerif-Regular uni:no), so both pdftotext
AND pdfplumber decode it as a space". Measured on collabra.90203 p.1:

- NotoSerif-Regular carries 561 char objects on that page and ALL 561 are the SPACE
  character -- it is the document's space font, not a symbol font.
- Its space widths are 2.08-3.90pt (mean 2.43); ZERO exceed 5pt, while the symbol's
  ink spans 7.98pt. No NotoSerif space is wide enough to be the symbol.
- The only char object near the gap is a NotoSerif space at x0=229.97 -- the ordinary
  space BEFORE the '=' at x=232.31, i.e. after the symbol, not in place of it.
- The symbol is 4 filled bezier curves (fill=True, no fontname) with NO char object.

So the verdict (OCR/shape-recognition tier for body prose) is RIGHT, but the stated
mechanism is REFUTED. Codex on why that still causes harm: the rationale teaches the
wrong failure mode, so a consumer would attempt ToUnicode recovery, glyph-name
mapping, extractor tuning or post-processing NotoSerif spaces -- all of which target
the ordinary space before '=' and can never recover drawn curves. The distinction
that matters is "text encoded badly" vs "ink that is not text".

PROPAGATION CONFIRMED. REPLY_TO_DOCPLUCK_2026-06-26 records ESCIcheck replying "we
confirmed your OCR-tier won't-fix: the prose reads '( = .000...)' with no eta
anywhere" -- the identical circular check. A wrong rationale crossed the repo
boundary and was ratified by the receiving project using the same flawed method.
That is exactly the shape this audit exists to catch.

Both documents now carry correction blocks (in ESCIcheckapp, a separate repo). The
table-side fields.eta2 binding is unaffected and remains correct. A deterministic
vector-path recogniser remains a viable NON-OCR route.

lines that made the block recognisable as furniture and welds the residue into

Rule 20 says "survey the corpus before you write a threshold". Run 5 obeyed it
and still got the survey wrong TWICE, in opposite directions, so the rule needed
the missing half: how to build a survey whose number means anything.

(a) Survey through the REAL entry point. The W0i survey fed raw pdftotext lines

    and reported ~85 hits in 10 papers -- including a paper's TITLE. The
    production render for that same paper had ZERO. Overstated ~10x; reporting it

    returned zero firings corpus-wide -- a comfortable all-clear that was pure
    artifact (W0d runs whole-document; the raw-text channel puts each cell on its
    own line, so an estimate and its CI never share a line).

(c) Prefer a GUARD-DIFF over a hit count: render twice with the change toggled,

    evidence. When a full double-render is too slow, pre-filter by a stated
    criterion and report BOTH numbers so coverage stays auditable.

you are detecting occurs on exactly ONE row, no vote/follower/corroboration rule
can recover it. Counting the populated occurrences first would have saved two

far too weak to found a threshold on, and per-column corroboration explains why:

    x=36.0 -> 15/15    x=284.7 -> 4/15    x=369.3 -> 3/15
    x=442.8 -> 1/15    x=549.8 -> 0/15  <- the P-value column

The rightmost column has ZERO corroboration anywhere in the table. Rel. risk and
P value are populated on exactly ONE row (the aggregate); the other 11 are
indented sub-rows that legitimately leave them blank. No vote-, follower-, or
corroboration-based rule can recover a column that occurs once -- the repetition
those algorithms need is not in the document.

So a geometry-only repair is impossible for this class, which retires the whole
family of attempts rather than inviting a fifth. What remains viable is evidence
from outside the geometry: header-TEXT typing (the header cells are recognisable
statistic labels, so they declare the column count directly), gated to
caption-anchored regions so it cannot fire on the ~1,700 prose pages the earlier
survey surfaced; or feeding header-derived x-positions to Camelot as explicit
columns. Both still need the 101-PDF guard-diff and canary sweep.

Records the cheap early check that would have saved two prototypes: count how
many rows populate the missing column; if it is 1, no geometric rule applies.

highlights.message: docs(findings): header-seeding PROTOTYPED then REJECTED by the corpus survey
highlights.body:
The proposed repair for plos_med T3's lost statistics columns -- seed boundaries
from the widest row, since the header declares every column -- was prototyped and
recovers the 5-column grid exactly. The vote tally shows the defect in one line:
the four TRUE boundaries carry 5, 13, 2 and 2 votes against a threshold of 7, so
exactly one clears it and the rule deletes all four.

The corpus survey then killed the fix. Scanning all 152 PDFs for the shape returns
1,707 pages, dominated by ordinary PROSE (modal=1 widest=4 wide_rows=1/22).
Inspecting one directly shows the "widest row" is a PAGE FOOTER --
"JAMANetworkOpen.2023;6(5): | (Reprinted) | May31,2023 | 10/12" -- above a
REFERENCES list. Seeding from it would fabricate a 4-column table out of a
bibliography on ~1,700 pages; the tail ("lost 29 columns") is the same artifact.

So the failing signal is not sparsity but IDENTITY: which row is actually a
header. A viable fix must establish that first (inside a caption-anchored region,
followed by data rows sharing its column starts -- _row_is_header is the natural
home) and be re-measured against this same 1,707-page population.

Second geometric shortcut rejected for this defect class, fourth across the
row-cluster family. Each looked excellent on its motivating paper; measurement,
not review, killed them. Recorded as a project lesson: print the winning row's
TEXT, not just its column count -- a footer, a running header and a wrapped
caption all look like "wide rows" to geometry.

highlights.message: fix(normalize): refuse a sign flip against a CI that cannot hold a negative (v2.4.123)
highlights.body:
docpluck rendered an IMPOSSIBLE F-statistic. maier Table 9's row is

    Target article | 1, 114 | 2.00 | .16 | N/A | .02 | [.00, .09]

-- an F, its p, its partial eta-squared, and the CI OF THE ETA-SQUARED. W0d
(recover_minus_via_ci_pairing) repairs a font corruption where a minus is read
as '2', accepting the flip when the corrected value lands inside a paired CI and
the literal does not. It paired the F-statistic with the eta-squared's CI: -.00
is inside [.00, .09] and 2.00 is not, so it fired, and the render carried

    F = -.00

An F-statistic is a ratio of sums of squares -- non-negative by construction --
so the output was not merely wrong but arithmetically impossible. Both text
channels confirm the source reads 2.00; the library manufactured the sign.

Fix: refuse the pairing when the CI's LOWER bound is >= 0. A wholly non-negative
interval cannot contain a negative, so containment is satisfiable only
degenerately (-.00 clipping the zero edge), which is evidence of MIS-PAIRING
rather than corruption. Keying on the interval's arithmetic instead of on F
specifically covers every non-negative statistic that can sit beside a
non-negative CI (F, chi-square, R2, eta2, odds ratios, variance components)
without enumerating them, and cannot disarm a genuine recovery -- a truly
negative estimate always has a CI admitting negatives.

Evidence:
- tests written against the unfixed code and watched FAIL, then pass;
- all 31 pre-existing W0d tests stay green, incl. the efendic B-column
  recoveries the rule exists for;
- corpus guard-diff, all 152 PDFs rendered twice (guard on vs off):
  2 false positives removed (the maier article and its ESCIcheck duplicate),
  0 regressions, every other paper byte-identical;
- suite 1962 passed, 3 xfail (the P1 table defects stay armed).

Companion to the REJECTED W0b-col recovery: that failed because column consensus
is not per-record evidence. This is the converse -- per-record containment IS the
right evidence, but only when the record paired is the right one. A containment
test silently assumes the CI belongs to the token it pairs with; verify that is
arithmetically possible first.

Found by the run-5 canary audit against the AI multimodal gold.

highlights.message: docs(findings): measure WHY plos_med T3 loses its columns — hierarchical sub-rows
highlights.body:
Probing _find_stable_column_boundaries on the real Table-3 band replaces the
earlier speculation (which guessed at midpoint scatter and the region path) with
a measurement, and it kills the proposed fix:

  WORD path: valid_rows=13 threshold=7 -> stable boundaries: [] -> 1 column
  BUCKETED(3/5/8pt): still 2 columns

The word path finds ZERO stable boundaries, so the region path is NOT the
culprit. The cause is the table's shape: Table 3 is hierarchical -- the header
and one aggregate row carry all 5 columns, while 11 of 13 rows are indented
sub-rows carrying only 3 (desaturation | 3/5 | 1/4). The Rel. risk and P value
columns appear in 2/13 rows = 15%, far below COLUMN_STABILITY_FRACTION = 0.6, so
they can never reach the vote threshold. Bucketing cannot help -- the votes do
not exist to be bucketed.

Lowering the fraction is explicitly NOT the fix (rule 20): 0.6 guards against
spurious boundaries from ragged prose rows, and a threshold admitting a 15%
column admits noise corpus-wide. The correct signature is that a column declared
by the HEADER is real even when most rows leave it empty -- seed boundaries from
the header rather than letting a majority vote delete them. That is an algorithm
change to a shared detector, so it gets its own gated cycle.

Also removes the now-superseded speculative section so the doc does not
contradict its own measurement, and records the class as a project lesson: a
stability-fraction vote assumes every column is populated in most rows, which
hierarchical/sub-row tables (common in clinical papers) violate by construction --
and the failure is silent, looking like a complete table with fewer columns.

highlights.message: docs(findings): plos_med T3/T5 silently drop their statistics columns (capture layer)

The data IS present and clean in BOTH text channels -- the layout channel has

plain auto-detect returns a 7x2 grid with all four data columns crushed into one

Camelot returns a degenerate one) is explicitly the not-yet-wired change flagged

highlights.message: docs(findings): one typographic heading level rendered at two markdown levels
highlights.body:
The run-5 cycle-1 audit filed 4 SECTION-BOUNDARY findings claiming chan_feldman's
'Interpersonal forgiveness' et al. should be ## not ###. Checking the source PDF's
typography DISPROVES that claim: those headings are MyriadPro-BoldIt 10.0pt while
Method/Results/Discussion are MyriadPro-Bold 10.5pt -- a different font and size, so
### is defensible and the gold's flat ## is the less faithful rendering. Acting on
the audit would have meant promoting correct output to match a flattened gold.

Disproving it surfaced a REAL defect the audit missed: docpluck splits ONE
typographic level across TWO markdown levels with no typographic basis. Background,
Original hypotheses, and Evaluation criteria render as ## while Interpersonal
forgiveness, Pre-registration, Power analysis and Participants render as ### -- all
of them BoldIt 10.0pt at x0=48.0. Background and Interpersonal forgiveness are
typographically indistinguishable and land on different levels, so the rendered
hierarchy is not a faithful model of the document.

Filed rather than fixed: the inconsistency is unambiguous, but which tier maps to
## is a product decision (mapping tier-2 uniformly to ### is typographically
faithful but demotes Background, which golds and readers expect at ##). Heading
promotion is also a shared code path with a history of corpus-wide regressions, so
any fix needs a heading-only guard-diff plus the 8-canary sweep.

Also re-scopes the broad-read "furniture leak" class to B6 in TRIAGE: 11 of 13
instances are mid-sentence column splices, not own-line strippable furniture, and
imada's 'irrespective of the Introduction' exists in NEITHER text channel.

highlights.message: fix(normalize): a range bound is a number, not an interaction operator (v2.4.122)
highlights.body:
W0i's x-as-3 glyph recovery was rewriting RANGE BOUNDS as an operator inside
Camelot table cells. chan_feldman's Table-2 note rendered

    "Avoidance behaviour scores ranged from x to 15"

for a source that reads "from 3 to 15" -- the library DELETED a published scale
bound and wrote an operator in its place. Both text channels confirm the source
says 3; the raw-text channel rendered the same sentence correctly a hundred
lines earlier, so one document carried the same fact right and wrong at once.

Not paper-specific: any "from 3 to N" / "between 3 and N" reaching a table cell
was affected, in any publisher's paper.

Root cause: W0i's only pre-digit guard was _TIMES_REFERENCE_WORD_RE, a list of
reference NOUNS (Model|Study|Table|Figure|...) that makes "Model 3 predictor" a
genuine ordinal. "from" is not a reference noun, so the guard had nothing to
say, while "from 3 to" matches W0i's letter-space-3-space-letter signature
exactly. A vocabulary list cannot defend a grammatical position -- it is always
missing the next word.

Fix: guard on the grammatical FRAME instead. A range is from|between BEFORE the
digit AND to|and|through|until AFTER it, with BOTH halves required -- a lone
trailing "to" could be a wrapped predictor ("Attitude 3 to risk"), and a lone
leading "from" is likewise ambiguous. A frame generalises across publishers.

Evidence:
- new tests written against the unfixed code and watched FAIL, then pass;
- full-corpus pdftotext sweep (all 152 PDFs): 8 range-frame-with-3 sites across
  5 distinct articles, out of 380 range frames overall -- all 5 pinned as
  regression cases. The sweep is why the guard covers "between ... and": maier's
  Bayes factors and bmc_med_3's lesion diameters use it, and a from-only guard
  would have left them exposed;
- targeted production-path guard-diff (each paper rendered twice, guard on vs
  off, so every difference is attributable to this change): 1 false positive
  removed, 0 regressions, all 8 canaries byte-identical;
- suite: 1959 passed, 3 xfail (the two P1 pinned table defects stay armed).

Found by the run-5 cycle-1 canary audit against the AI multimodal gold.

highlights.message: docpluck-iterate: add hard rule 20 — survey the corpus before writing a threshold
highlights.body:
The run-4 v2.4.120/121 session's most expensive mistake and its most valuable
save both trace to this missing rule. The skill had no guidance to validate a
threshold/ratio/signature against the corpus BEFORE implementing it.

Cost when absent: the _cluster_into_rows anchor-relative fix looked excellent on
its motivating paper (chan_feldman T3 3->22 rows, T2 0->108 cells) and broke 9
real-PDF tests, because a legitimate row can be 94pt tall (xiao T4 r2).

Value when applied: four geometric discriminators (row span, max internal gap,
distinct_y, sub-line width fraction) were each falsified in minutes against the
101-PDF corpus instead of via a revert.

The rule also encodes the label-verification half, which is where the real trap
sits: hand-picked extremes ALWAYS separate, so only the decision band matters,
and labelling by provenance is a guess. Verifying the band's labels by reading
them reversed this session's conclusion TWICE before the third reading settled
it. And it requires reporting the MARGIN, not just the ordering — a correct
ordering with a 0.019 gap on six points is a rejection, not a fix.

Companion to rule 16: rule 16 says key on a structural signature; rule 20 says
prove the signature actually discriminates before shipping it.

Purely additive (2 insertions, 0 deletions). The concurrent session's
uncommitted Dropbox->Vibe path edit in this same file is deliberately NOT
included and remains in the working tree.

highlights.message: docs(findings): 4 geometric chain-merge discriminators tested and rejected; period-aware column overlap is the best candidate but still unsafe
highlights.body:
Continues the corpus-driven falsification of the row-cluster chain-merge fix.

REJECTED (all measured corpus-wide or on verified cases):
  - row span:            legit rows reach 94pt+ (xiao T4 r2)
  - max internal y-gap:  9.0pt legit vs 9.5pt chain — indistinguishable
  - distinct_y count:    continuous 2->50, classes interleave (legit 26 > chain 23)
  - subline width frac:  both classes 0.42-0.54, chain sits BETWEEN legit rows
                         (raw widths looked separable, 202-238 vs 84-150, but the
                         chain-merge regions are simply wider — normalising kills it)
  - start_at_left:       46% in BOTH classes

BEST CANDIDATE, still unsafe: column-boundary consistency. Mean Jaccard of
x-start buckets between CONSECUTIVE sub-lines gives chain 0.008-0.023 vs legit
0.21-0.28 — except xiao T4 r2 scores 0.017, deep in the chain band. That is the
exact row whose mis-splitting broke 9 tests, so this variant would repeat the
failure. It alternates data lines with CI-continuation lines, so consecutive
sub-lines never share columns but the pattern is strictly PERIODIC.

A period-aware variant (best mean Jaccard over lags 1-3) fixes xiao (0.692) and
separates the rest — but ip_feldman T10 r1 (chain) reaches 0.251 against chan T6
r2 (legit) at 0.270. A 0.019 margin on six hand-picked rows will not survive the
corpus; it needs the same survey that killed distinct_y, over rows whose class is
VERIFIED rather than assumed, and must be rejected if the margin does not widen.

Explicit guidance added: do NOT attempt a fifth geometric threshold. Remaining
viable directions are content typing and split-then-re-merge on column occupancy.

No library code changes.
